Niger is a Saharan African nation with numerous ethnic groups: Hausa, Taureg, Fulani, Zarma, Wodaabe, Sagolo, Kanori, Sogha, Djerma, etc. What ethnic group is Bozo? The Bozo are a West African ethnic group located predominantly along the Niger River in Mali. The name Bozo is thought to derive from Bambara bo-so "straw house"; the people accept it as referring to the whole of the ethnic group but use more specific clan names such as Sorogoye, Hain, and Tieye themselves. Who are the Bozo people? The Bozo people are experts in living on the waterside and making a living from fishing. According to legend, they are descendants of Faro, the water spirit and creator god, and are seen as the inventors of the masquerade tradition in Mali. Where did Bozo culture come from? Aspects of Bozo culture took shape under the 10th century Ghana Empire, when the Bozo took possession of the banks of the Niger. The Bozo were the founders of the Malian cities of Djenné and Mopti. Though the Bozo are predominantly Muslim, they preserve a number of animist traditions as well. Are there different types of Bozo language?
